title: Galileo Project instruments on Harvard College Observatory

tellings.quote: I received thousands of emails from people that are excited to contribute to the project. By now, we have more than a hundred scientists engaged in the Galileo Project. We are purchasing the instrumentation that we will place on the roof of the Harvard College Observatory in the coming months.

tellings.difference: Eric Weinstein tells it second hand and only in passing, saying Loeb was setting up an effort at Harvard. He does not name the project and leaves out the instruments, the observatory roof and the number of scientists.
tellings.link_reason: Both describe Avi Loeb's 2021 Harvard program to study UAP, the Galileo Project. The story is recorded as a program, and its telling covers the project's setup (scientists joining, instruments being bought) as well as the instruments.

as_told.title: Galileo Project sensors at Harvard Observatory

plain: A Harvard scientist named Avi Loeb said in early 2022 that his new research effort, the Galileo Project, which studies unexplained objects in the sky, had drawn thousands of excited emails and more than a hundred scientists. He said they were buying instruments to put on the roof of the Harvard College Observatory in the coming months, which would mean a major university looking at the question directly. Another researcher, Eric Weinstein, mentioned it in passing a few weeks later, saying only that Loeb was setting something up at Harvard.
